Thanks — ran the numbers and attached a couple of simple models (spreadsheet stub). Two concise options:

Option A — Anchored daily allowance (simpler billing):
- Anchor: 60M tokens/day for 7 days (420M tokens total anchor) billed upfront at discounted microtrial rate $0.0006/token -> anchor fee $252
- Overage: any usage above anchor billed at pay-as-you-go retail $0.0009/token; expected overage window pricing applies
- Advantages: predictable invoice amount, simple reconciliation for procurement

Option B — Volume-triggered escrow (conditional release):
- Luminate deposits $400 upfront to an escrow account at contract start
- If total weekly volume >= 350M tokens (the threshold), Redwood releases 80% of escrow and applies remaining 20% as credit against overage billing. If threshold not met, 90% refunded after 14 days, 10% retained for administrative/settlement fees.
- Advantages: aligns incentives to hit usage thresholds; procurement keeps leverage

Discounts for burst commitment: we can offer a temporary 10% off overage rate for up to 2 burst days if Luminate commits to pre-declaring burst windows 48 hours ahead. That would make the burst-rate for those days $0.00081/token instead of $0.0009.

I've attached the luminate-multi-tier-sku.xlsx (stub) showing line items and example math for your expected and burst profiles. Also flagged the settlement timeline for the escrow flow so legal can check refund windows.

Ben

Hi procurement team —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Summarizing action items and our position so we can get the SOW executed this week:

1) Escrow admin: Redwood is fine with a neutral third-party escrow agent (we typically use EscrowCo for trial flows). We'll include EscrowCo as the default; if Luminate prefers a different auditor/agent, we can accommodate.
2) Retained percentage: we can reduce the administrative holdback to 5% if Luminate signs a non-binding LOI to target production conversion inside 90 days. We'll capture the LOI language as a 1-paragraph attachment to the SOW.
3) Net terms: Redwood can accept net-30 on the anchor only with a PO + signed SOW and a credit check. Otherwise, standard is upfront for anchors. If procurement needs net-30 immediately, we can route to finance for approval; expect a 48–72 hour turnaround.

Decision request for Luminate: do you prefer we move forward with Option A (Anchored daily allowance, net-30 on PO) or Option B (Escrow with EscrowCo + 5% holdback tied to LOI)? If you pick Option A we will: (a) attach the SOW draft (SOW-microtrial-draft.pdf stub) to the DocuSign envelope, (b) auto-populate the invoice for the anchor at $252, and (c) schedule the kickoff for Mon 12/7.

If the team prefers a quick call to finalize, I have an 11–11:30 PST window Monday or a 4–4:30 PST window Friday.

Thanks — we'll move fast once you confirm.

Best,
